speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions, specifically noting their shape, color, and any changes in size over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the non-healing nature and location of the penile lesion are concerning. Given your smoking history and the lesion's characteristics, have you noticed any pain, bleeding, or discharge from either site? Also, when did you first notice these lesions, and have they changed in size or color since then?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (Penile and Digit)

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of penile lesion and left middle finger lesion; Complete Blood Count and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy images of both lesions to assess for ulceration and keratin pearls.
